title: Negative operands crash inside tokenize()
body:
Same symptom as the other negative-number report, but on 0.0.9 the crash comes out of the tokenizer, which converted tokens as it scanned them. `tokenize` calls `int()` on the bare `-` and dies there.

Steps to reproduce:

```bash
pip install pytest
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluate.py -x
```

Output:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_evaluate.py", line 13, in test_negative_operand
    assert evaluate("2 + -3") == -1
  File "src/tinycalc/evaluate.py", line 12, in tokenize
    return [int(tok) for tok in _TOKEN.findall(expr)]
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-'
```

Expected: the tokenizer keeps `-3` as one token instead of calling `int("-")`.
